title: Which other twin primes lie between 1 and 100?
description: Neighbouring primes in the list are compared, and the pairs that are two apart are picked out. Three and five and seventeen and nineteen are given, and six more pairs are found.
teaching_notes: One idea: twin primes are neighbouring primes that are two apart, so they are found by scanning the list for a gap of two. Watch for students who skip five and seven because five has already been used in a pair.

video_script.why: The child scans the list of primes for neighbouring pairs that are two apart.
video_script.substitution: Go along the list of primes and mark each neighbouring pair that is two apart.
video_script.anchor: The list of primes up to 100 with the gap marked between each neighbouring pair
video_script.payoff_line: There are six more twin prime pairs below a hundred.

final_answer.value: 5 and 7, 11 and 13, 29 and 31, 41 and 43, 59 and 61, 71 and 73
final_answer.spoken: six more twin prime pairs lie below a hundred

maths_rules: other neighbouring pairs are further apart, for example 11 - 7 = 4 and 29 - 23 = 6
video_script.design: The row of primes is scanned from left to right; a neighbouring pair that is two apart lights up teal and the others stay grey.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about twin primes.
<bookmark mark='twin'/>Twin primes are two primes that are two apart, such as three and five, or seventeen and nineteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the other twin primes between one and a hundred.

narration: <bookmark mark='neigh'/>We read neighbouring primes from the list that the circling and crossing out gave us.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>For each pair, take away the smaller prime from the bigger one, and see if two is left.

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step one, scan the list from the front. Seven take away five is two, so five and seven are twin primes.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Thirteen take away eleven is two, so eleven and thirteen are twin primes.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>Thirty one take away twenty nine is two, so those two are twin primes as well.

marks.forty: forty one and forty three light up with a gap of two
marks.fifty: fifty nine and sixty one light up with a gap of two
marks.seventy: seventy one and seventy three light up with a gap of two

narration: <bookmark mark='forty'/>Step two, keep scanning. Forty one and forty three are two apart.
<bookmark mark='fifty'/>Fifty nine and sixty one are two apart.
<bookmark mark='seventy'/>Seventy one and seventy three are two apart.

beats.on_screen: Check: 11 − 7 = 4 and 29 − 23 = 6 are not 2; 6 new pairs plus the given 3, 5 and 17, 19

marks.far: the pairs seven and eleven, and twenty three and twenty nine, are shown further apart
marks.six: the six new pairs are counted beside the two given pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='far'/>Step three, check the other neighbours. Seven and eleven are four apart, and twenty three and twenty nine are six apart.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Such pairs are not twin primes, so we have six new pairs.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 5 and 7, 11 and 13, 29 and 31, 41 and 43, 59 and 61, 71 and 73

marks.first: the first three pairs light up
marks.second: the last three pairs light up

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>There are six more twin prime pairs below a hundred.
<bookmark mark='first'/>They are five and seven, eleven and thirteen, and twenty nine and thirty one.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Then come forty one and forty three, fifty nine and sixty one, seventy one and seventy three.
